verify: cd host && npx vitest run test/vfs/default-mounts.test.ts >/dev/null 2>&1

trials.name: a browser scratch mount the kernel does not serve is silently ignored
an IMAGE mount is refused too, so no boot resolves its spec
the tmpfs filter stops running, so the kernel's own prefixes are refused

_comment: The browser host has no filesystem to mount. `/` is the kernel's since the Phase 5 cutover, the eight prefixes the in-kernel tmpfs owns are filtered out before this looks, and what is left is a scratch mount at a path nothing can back -- so it is refused rather than dropped. Silently dropping it is the failure that matters: the caller believes it declared a mount, the kernel never sees one, and the divergence surfaces later as a missing directory rather than as a rejected spec. The third trial guards the other direction, because a filter that stopped running would refuse the very prefixes the kernel serves and break every boot. Node is deliberately NOT symmetric here: it backs such a mount with a HostFileSystem over a real session directory, because session seed trees must land below a surviving scratch mount and `/run/kandelo-run` is the kernel's own canonical example of a foreign mount.
